Authentication

The relay key, its scopes, and what the router answers when the key is missing or short of a scope.

Every door under /v1 takes a relay key as a bearer token: Authorization: Bearer mrk_<prefix>_<secret>. A missing, malformed, unknown, revoked or expired key all get the same answer, a 401 with code invalid_api_key and a WWW-Authenticate header, so the answer never confirms which keys exist.

Scopes

A key carries scopes. A door that needs a scope the key lacks answers 403 with code insufficient_scope, and the answer names the scope it wanted in massrelay.requiredScope. The explain door, for one, needs the explain scope.

Where keys come from

A workspace member with the right role creates, limits and revokes keys on the Keys page of the console. A key has a policy of its own (allowed models, a budget envelope, a guardrail), set through the console. The secret is shown once, when the key is created.

Provisioning keys for your users

A workspace admin can issue a management key: a key with the keys:manage scope, created on the Keys page with an explicit confirmation. It does one thing, which is to mint, list, change and revoke keys for your own users under /v1/management/keys.

| Call | What it does | |---|---| | POST /v1/management/keys | Mints a key. Body: scopes (any of chat, models, explain; default chat), label, endUser, expiresAt (ISO 8601), budgetEnvelopeId. The answer carries the key once, with Cache-Control: no-store. | | GET /v1/management/keys | The keys this management key minted. Never a secret or a hash. | | GET /v1/management/keys/{id} | One of them. | | PATCH /v1/management/keys/{id} | Sets expiresAt and/or budgetEnvelopeId. An expiry cannot be cleared. | | DELETE /v1/management/keys/{id} | Revokes the key. The row stays; a second call keeps the first time. |

A provisioned key never carries keys:manage (400 scope_not_delegable), is never an L0 or bring-your-own-upstream key (400 field_not_allowed), and inherits the management key's policy profile and budget envelope unless you name another envelope of the same workspace (400 envelope_not_found otherwise). Your workspace's key ceiling applies: past it the answer is 409 key_limit, and massrelay.limit and massrelay.active say where you stand. A key that is not yours to manage (another management key's, another workspace's, one made in the console) answers 404, the same as a key that does not exist. If the workspace holds these actions for review, a write answers 202 with a proposalId and changes nothing.

Rate-limit headers

Read your key's scopes and spend back with GET /v1/key (see Credits and usage). X-RateLimit-* headers on every answer are coming with a limiter lane; until then a request over the limit answers 429 with a Retry-After header; see Limits.

Console doors

The console's own doors under /api take a signed-in session, not a relay key. The reference states, for every door, which of the two it takes.
